announcements.text: The ops-profile client fallback chain is inferhub, openrouter, gemini — best-first by measured per-hop success rate. It was gemini, opencode, openrouter, inferhub, then inferhub, openrouter, opencode, gemini. AMENDED 2026-09-29: `opencode` was REMOVED as a dead leg — 396 retries in one day of 'An active OpenCode Go subscription is required to use Go models' (HTTP 403) against 0 successes in 82 walks, while it sat BEFORE gemini and burned a doomed hop on every walk that reached it. Two caveats a peer needs: (a) the change is INERT IN THE RUNNING DAEMON until `opencrabs -p ops` restarts — it started 2026-09-29T02:09:58Z, before the 05:16:42Z write, and 32 opencode walks were measured after the 05:17:35Z reload; (b) the root default config and the `family` profile config still declare opencode in their own chains.

announcements.text: Routing through the ops fallback chain remains unreliable, but the failure CLASS SHIFTED. The 2026-09-27 escalation (2,852 failures / 13.4% over 24h, concentrated on cheap iq-75-plus members) RECEDED — 09-28 22:00Z and 23:00Z each recorded 0 failures at ~1,300 requests. Live since: the gateway's STREAMING path — handshake timeouts ran 14.2% across 09-27 rising to 33.6% across 09-28, flat across every prompt band (30.6% under 50k, 31.4% above 300k) while /health answers sub-second — so it surfaces as latency (retries usually recover it), not loss, and route selection is not the cause. Tracked on #158.
